## Unblocked — `pm:blocked` → `pm:queue`. Blocker #6270 closed by PR #6591, merged 2026-08-27T12:47:33Z.

`domain:ui` @ objectui execution seat, PM session `session_01CRJge11jso9TpXRWFt1Z49`, round 1. Label moved in the same stroke as this comment; `Blocked-by: #6270` in the body is now discharged.

### File-face re-verification on the merged ref — done, and it matters here

⭐ The unlock scan's third duty is the one most often skipped: **the merge that closed the blocker is the merge most likely to have quietly done this card's work too.** Checked rather than assumed.

It did **not**, and the reason is structural: PR #6591 changed **three files** — `packages/react/src/SchemaRenderer.tsx`, one new test under `packages/react`, and a changeset. It did not touch `packages/plugin-map`, and it did not touch any consumer's effect dependency array. That is not incidental — the dispatch order for #6270 explicitly forbade touching downstream renderers' memo keys, and the dev followed it and flagged the conflict rather than widening. So this card's work is entirely unstarted, exactly as its body records.

### ⚠️ What changed about this card's premise — read this before dispatching it

PR #6591 **strengthens** the argument for doing this work rather than weakening it, and the distinction is easy to get backwards:

> #6591 makes the schema identity **stable**. It does not make it **guaranteed**.

`useMemo` carries no semantic guarantee — React is permitted to discard a memo cache and recompute. A fetch effect keyed on a memoised object identity is therefore correct only for as long as that cache happens to survive. #6591 removed the *routine* churn (a fresh object on every parent render, and on every mount via the registry `forceUpdate()`); it did not remove the *dependence on cache survival*. This card is what removes that.

⛔ So do not read "the identity is stable now" as "this card is moot." A reviewer or a dev who measures stability today will find it, and that measurement is **not** evidence against this card.

### Constraints carried forward, unchanged

- ⛔ The `useRef` / stable-key identity hack stays forbidden (the #6018 ruling).
- The acceptance direction is **"the effect no longer reads an object identity"**. ⭐ A pin that only proves the identity is stable today does not test this card — the test has to stay green when the memo cache is **deliberately discarded**. That is the review question to hold this to.
- The file face is a **census, not an inherited claim**: `packages/plugin-map` is the one known member; the complete set is "every renderer whose fetch effect deps carry a memoised config object". Measure it with a positive control before believing any zero in it. `packages/react/src/SchemaRenderer.tsx` is expected to need no further change.

Not dispatched this round: in-flight is at the standing cap of 3 (#6595 · #6593 · #6236). This card joins the queue behind #6598, which is first out when a slot opens.

The two things that decide whether this card is done right are already written on it, and both go into the dispatch order **verbatim**, as triage asked:

1. ⭐ **The acceptance direction is "the effect no longer reads an object identity."** ⛔ A pin that only proves the identity is stable today **does not test this card**. 2. ⭐ **The file face is a census, not an inherited claim.** `packages/plugin-map` is the one *known* member; the real set is *every renderer whose fetch effect deps carry a memoised config object*. Measure it with a **positive control** before believing any zero in it — `git ls-tree` the paths first, and make the query shape able to produce a non-zero.

⚠️ **The premise trap, restated because it is easy to get backwards.** PR #6591 made the schema identity **stable**; it did **not** make it **guaranteed**. `useMemo` carries no semantic guarantee — React may discard a memo cache and recompute, and a fetch effect keyed on a memoised identity is correct only while that cache survives. ⛔ So a dev who measures stability today **will find it**, and that measurement is **not** evidence this card is moot. #6591 removed the routine churn; this card removes the dependence on cache survival.

⛔ The `useRef` / stable-key identity hack stays **forbidden** — the #6018 ruling, unchanged.

⚠️ Fence note for the census: three cards are in flight on adjacent surfaces right now — `components/src/renderers/overlay/**` + `types/overlay.ts` (#6523+#6346), `plugin-dashboard` / `plugin-grid` / `types` (#6597), and `packages/react` (PR #6690, awaiting merge). If the census reaches into any of those, **stop and report the overlap** rather than editing across it. `packages/react/src/SchemaRenderer.tsx` is expected to need no further change.

Inherited measurements, ⛔ not to be re-derived but worth re-locating on the current ref: `mapConfig` was keyed on `[schema]` by #5976 (PR #6016, `538ed9246`); `dataConfig` by #6018 (PR #6266, `2aa2c226a`).

ACCEPT — PR #6698, head `8da309855`, flipped ready. **Ruling on the open question: option A** — the `ObjectTree` record effect gets a small follow-up card once #6696 merges. Reasoning below.

Three renderers re-keyed onto the primitives they actually read (`provider` / `object` / `items`): `ObjectMap`, `ObjectCalendar`, `ObjectGantt`.

## ⭐⭐ The prediction miss is the most valuable thing in this report

The ablation predicted all four discard-pins would go red pre-fix. **`ObjectCalendar`'s first construction passed even pre-fix** — and the root cause is the interesting part:

> `ObjectCalendar`'s own `dataConfig` memo is **already primitive-keyed by #6018**, so that trigger never recomputed it.

⇒ The chosen trigger could not discriminate, because an **earlier fix had already removed the recompute path it depended on**. The dev reported the miss, re-derived a trigger that varies `schema.data` by reference instead, and confirmed *that* one goes red pre-fix.

⭐ Forcing the prediction here would have shipped a pin that **cannot fail** — green forever, guarding nothing, indistinguishable from a working guard. That is the exact failure class this lane keeps meeting from the other direction, and it is the second time this week a dev has caught it by refusing to accept a convenient green. It goes in the seat post as: **a trigger that stops discriminating because a previous fix removed its path is not a passing test — it is a dead pin.**

## The census was done as a census

Positive-controlled on the known `plugin-map` member, and it found **more** than the card's one known name: `ObjectTree` and `plugin-grid` are members too. Both correctly left alone — `plugin-grid` fenced by #6597, and `ObjectTree` for the reason below.

⭐ Three further effects **outside** the `dataConfig` family with the same structural hazard (`plugin-detail/RelatedList.tsx`, `components/renderers/layout/containers.tsx`, `plugin-list/ListView.tsx`) were **filed as #6697 rather than folded in**. Correct: the card's scope is the `dataConfig` family, and widening a hardening refactor to every memo-keyed effect in the repo is how a bounded card becomes unreviewable.

## ⭐ The mid-flight fence collision was handled exactly right

`ObjectTree` was **implemented and then reverted out** of this branch after I relayed that PR #6696 was rewriting that same file. The RED/GREEN pair is preserved in the PR body as the record of what was measured before the surface turned contested.

⇒ That is the correct outcome of a live fence collision: the measurement is kept, the edit is dropped, and nothing is silently raced. It also validates the relay — the two seats would otherwise have collided on `ObjectTree.tsx` inside the same ten minutes.

## The ruling: A, and why

The residual is `ObjectTree`'s **record** effect at `:468`, a confirmed census member.

⛔ **B (leave it) is refused.** This card's own census names `ObjectTree` as a member. Shipping a census that names a member the card then declines to fix leaves a documented gap that reads, to the next reader, exactly like an unmeasured one — the "declared but not kept" shape this lane spends its time removing. A card may legitimately not fix what it did not measure; it should not leave behind what it did.

**A is cheap and carries no shape uncertainty**: ~10 lines, one effect, mirroring a pattern this PR proved three times, and #6696's own body confirms the record effect's dependency list and gate placement are **untouched** by it. So the only thing to wait out is the merge itself.

⭐ And #6481's dev handed forward two facts the follow-up inherits: this PR's sibling already re-keyed `ObjectTree`'s **schema resolution** onto the primitive `schemaKey`, so **the record effect's `dataConfig` dep is the last one in that component**. The follow-up closes the component, not just an effect.

⇒ I will dispatch it once #6696 lands (armed, 29/29 green). ⛔ Not folded back into this card — this PR is green and reviewable as it stands, and reopening it to add a fourth renderer on a contested file would trade a clean landing for a merge race.

Lint invariance proved the right way: `eslint --format json` on the three shipped files, **`origin/main` content vs branch — 188 warnings / 0 errors on both sides**, zero new findings. Restorations verified by `git hash-object` against `git rev-parse HEAD:PATH` on all four blobs.
